title: Baton Rouge Fire Department recruiting new entry-level firefighters - NewsBreak
text:
By Khayla Gaston ,
9 hours ago
BATON ROUGE, La. (Louisiana First) — The Baton Rouge Fire Department is looking to hire a new class of entry-level firefighters as the city continues to grow and retirements create openings across the department.
BRFD officials say they’re working to fill 30 positions to ensure the department remains fully staffed and prepared to respond to emergencies.
“This is more than just a job. This is a calling,” said Billy Zachary, BRFD public information officer. “It’s a place where you forge camaraderie and teamwork. And you earn the trust of your peers as well as the trust of the city.”
The department said the next rookie academy begins May 18, but anyone interested must submit an application by the end of February.
The hiring process starts with the firefighter civil service exam through the Office of State Examiner. After receiving an eligible score, candidates must complete the Baton Rouge Fire Department entry-level application and submit the required documentation.
Officials say prior firefighting experience is not required.
“As far as experience, there’s no experience necessary,” Zachary said. “We’ll train them beginning on day one, you’re paid on day one of training, and we will transform them into a professional firefighter with an EMT certification.”
BRFD leaders said the academy is challenging and requires discipline, encouraging applicants to start preparing now.
“Don’t expect it to be easy,” Zachary said. “It is physically demanding, and we’re upfront about that. Start preparing now, exercise, and try to get in shape. Be ready to study and dedicate time to studying every day.”
Officials say they’re looking for people who can stay calm under pressure and are ready for the responsibility of protecting the community.
